sanskrit: trir yātudhānaḥ prasitiṃ ta etv ṛtaṃ yo agne anṛtena hanti | tam arciṣā sphūrjayañ jātavedaḥ samakṣam enaṃ gṛṇate ni vṛṅdhi ||
english: Thrice let the yātudhāna come within thy snare; he who smites the truth with falsehood, O Agni — him, crackling with thy flame, O Jātavedas, cut down before the eyes of him who praises thee.

sanskrit: yad agne adya mithunā śapāto yad vācas tṛṣṭaṃ janayanta rebhāḥ | manyor manasaḥ śaravyā jāyate yā tayā vidhya hṛdaye yātudhānān ||
english: What curse the two together hurl today, O Agni, what harsh word the chanters generate — the arrow that is born from wrath and from the mind: with that pierce the yātudhānas in the heart.

sanskrit: parā śṛṇīhi tapasā yātudhānān parāgne rakṣo harasā śṛṇīhi | parārciṣā mūradevāñ chṛṇīhi parāsutṛpaḥ śośucataḥ śṛṇīhi ||
english: Smite away the yātudhānas with thy heat; smite away the rakṣas with thy blaze, O Agni; smite away the foolish demons with thy flame; smite away those who would drink up the vital force as thou blazest forth.

sanskrit: parādya devā vṛjinaṃ śṛṇantu pratyag enaṃ śapathā yantu sṛṣṭāḥ | vācāstenaṃ śarava ṛcchantu marman viśvayaitu prasitiṃ yātudhānaḥ ||
english: Let the gods today cut off the crooked one; let the hurled curses fly back upon him; let the arrows strike the word-thief in the vital spot; let the yātudhāna enter thy noose from every side.

sanskrit: sanād agne mṛṇasi yātudhānān na tvā rakṣāṃsi pṛtanāsu jigyuḥ | anu daha sahamūrān kravyādo mā te hetyā mukṣata daivyāyāḥ ||
english: From of old, O Agni, thou dost crush the yātudhānas; the rakṣases have never conquered thee in battles. Burn down the flesh-eating fools along with their companions; let them not escape from thy divine weapon.

sanskrit: yaḥ pauruṣeyeṇa kraviṣā samaṅkte yo aśvyena paśunā yātudhānaḥ | yo aghnyāyā bharati kṣīram agne teṣāṃ śīrṣāṇi harasāpi vṛśca ||
english: The yātudhāna who defiles himself with human flesh, who does so with the flesh of horse or cattle beast, who carries off the milk of the inviolable cow, O Agni — hew off the heads of those with thy blaze.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarīṇaṃ paya usriyāyās tasya māsīd yātudhāno nṛcakṣaḥ | pīyūṣam agne yatamas titṛpsāt taṃ pratyañcam arciṣā vidhya marman ||
english: Whoever, gazing upon men, is a yātudhāna and would drink the year-long milk of the dappled cow, or the colostrum — whoever among them would satisfy himself therewith, O Agni, pierce that one head-on with thy flame in the vital spot.

sanskrit: viṣaṃ gavāṃ yātudhānāḥ pibantv ā vṛścantām aditaye durevāḥ | paraiṇān devaḥ savitā dadātu parā bhāgam oṣadhīnāṃ jayantām ||
english: Let the yātudhānas drink the poison of the cows; let those evil ones be cut down for Aditi. Let the god Savitā give them over utterly; let them forfeit their share in the plants.

sanskrit: tvaṃ no agne adharād udaktas tvaṃ paścād uta rakṣā purastāt | prati tye te ajarāsas tapiṣṭhā aghaśaṃsaṃ śośucato dahantu ||
english: Do thou, O Agni, guard us from below and from above, from behind, and protect us from in front. Let those ageless, most scorching flames of thine, blazing, burn the evil-proclaimer.

sanskrit: paścāt purastād adharād udaktaḥ kaviḥ kāvyena pari pāhy agne | sakhā sakhāyam ajaro jarimṇe agne martyām̐ amartyas tvaṃ naḥ ||
english: From behind and from before, from below and from above, guard us with the poet's wisdom, O Agni the poet. As a friend guards a friend against old age, O Agni, thou art immortal — guard us mortals.

sanskrit: tad agne cakṣuḥ prati dhehi rebhe śaphārujaṃ yena paśyasi yātudhānam | atharvavaj jyotiṣā daivyena [Bhatt. atharvava(j) satyaṃ dhūrvantam acitaṃ ny oṣa ||
english: That eye, O Agni, fix upon the chanter — the hoof-smashing one with which thou seest the yātudhāna. Like Atharvan, with the divine light, burn down completely that unwise one who harms the truth.

sanskrit: pari tvāgne puraṃ vayaṃ vipraṃ sahasya dhīmahi | dhṛṣadvarṇaṃ divedive hantāraṃ bhaṅgurāvatām ||
english: Around thee, O Agni, we place our thought as a stronghold, O wise one, O powerful one — bold-hued, day by day the slayer of the Bhaṅgurāvat demons.

sanskrit: vi jyotiṣā bṛhatā bhāty agnir āvir viśvāni kṛṇute mahitvā | prādevīr māyāḥ sahate durevāḥ śiśīte śṛṅge rakṣase vinikṣe ||
english: Agni blazes forth with great light; by his greatness he makes all things manifest. He overcomes the divine māyās and the evil ones; he sharpens his two horns to pierce the rakṣas.

sanskrit: agnī rakṣāṃsi sedhati śukraśocir amartyaḥ | śuciḥ pāvaka īḍyaḥ ||
english: Agni drives away the rakṣases, brilliant in radiance, immortal; pure, cleansing, worthy of invocation.

sanskrit: agne rakṣā ṇo aṃhasaḥ prati ṣma deva rīṣataḥ | tapiṣṭhair ajaro daha ||
english: O Agni, protect us from affliction; ward off, O god, those who would harm us. Ageless, burn them with thy most scorching flames.

sanskrit: ye te śṛṅge ajare jātavedas tigmaśocī brahmasaṃśite | tābhyāṃ durhārdam abhidāsantaṃ kimīdinaṃ pratyañcaṃ yātudhānaṃ jātavedo vi nikṣva ||
english: Those two ageless horns of thine, O Jātavedas, sharp-gleaming, whetted by sacred utterance — with those two pierce through the kimīdin who is hard-hearted, who would destroy, the yātudhāna who faces thee, O Jātavedas.

sanskrit: viṣeṇa bhaṅgurāvataḥ sam indra rakṣaso daha | agne śukreṇa śociṣā tapuragrebhir arcibhiḥ ||
english: Burn together the Bhaṅgurāvat rakṣas with thy poison, O Indra; O Agni, with thy brilliant radiance, with flames whose tips are burning hot.

sanskrit: praty agne mithunā daha yātudhānā kimīdinā | saṃ tvā śiśāmi jāgṛhy adabdhaṃ vipra manmabhiḥ ||
english: Burn down, O Agni, the yātudhāna and the kimīdin as a pair. I whet thee with hymns; be vigilant, O wise one, undeceived.

sanskrit: praty agne harasā haraḥ śṛṇīhi viśvataḥ prati | yātudhānasya rakṣaso balaṃ vi ruja vīryam ||
english: Smite down, O Agni, the blaze with thy fiery wrath, from every direction. Shatter the strength, the heroic power, of the yātudhāna rakṣas.

sanskrit: sādānveyaṃ pra mṛṇa rakṣa indra yātudhānakṣayaṇair mūraiḥ | etāv agne mithunā yātudhānā viṣvañcau mruktau harasā śayātām ||
english: Crush down utterly this one who dwells on the path, O Indra, O guardian, with the fools who destroy yātudhānas. Let these two yātudhānas as a pair, O Agni, lie dead and scattered in every direction, slain by thy blaze.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir naḥ pari pātu paścād utottarasmād adharād aghāyoḥ | indraḥ purastād uta madhyato naḥ sakhā sakhibhyo varīyaḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: Let Bṛhaspati guard us from behind and from the north, from below against the evil-doer. Let Indra guard us from in front and from the middle; let him, as a friend, make things more spacious for his friends.

sanskrit: indrāsomā tapataṃ rakṣa ubjataṃ ny arpayataṃ vṛṣaṇā tamovṛdhaḥ | parā śṛṇīhi tam acito ny oṣataṃ hataṃ nudethāṃ ni śiśītam atriṇaḥ ||
english: O Indra and Soma, scorch the rakṣas, press it down, cast it down, O ye two bulls who increase darkness. Smite it away, the senseless one; burn it utterly, smite it dead and thrust it away; sharpen yourselves against the devourers.

sanskrit: indrāsomā sam aghaśaṃsam abhy aghaṃ tapur yayastu carur agnivām̐ iva | brahmadviṣe kravyāde ghoracakṣase dveṣo dhattam anavāyaṃ kimīdine ||
english: O Indra and Soma, let burning heat go against the evil-proclaimer, against evil, like a cauldron full of fire. Lay irresistible hatred upon the brahman-hater, the flesh-eater, the fierce-eyed kimīdin.

sanskrit: indrāsomā duṣkṛto vavre antar anārambhaṇe tamasi pra vidhyatam | yathaiṣāṃ nātaḥ punar ekaś canodayat tad vām astu sahase manyumac chavaḥ ||
english: O Indra and Soma, pierce the evildoers through into the pit, into the darkness that has no handhold. So that not one of them may rise up from there again — let that be your power, full of wrath and might.

sanskrit: indrāsomā vartayataṃ divas pary agnitaptebhir yuvam aśmahanmabhiḥ | tapurvadhebhir ajarebhir atriṇo ni parśāne vidhyataṃ yantu nisvaram ||
english: O Indra and Soma, hurl down from heaven your stone-blows, heated in fire. With your burning, ageless weapons of death, pin the devourers in their ribs; let them go voiceless.

sanskrit: indrāsomā pra harataṃ divo vadhaṃ saṃ pṛthivyā aghaśaṃsāya tarhaṇam | ut takṣataṃ svaryaṃ parvatebhyo yena rakṣo vavṛdhānaṃ nijūrvathaḥ ||
english: O Indra and Soma, hurl the death-bolt from heaven; bring the crusher from the earth upon the evil-proclaimer. Hew out the solar timber from the mountains with which you two crush down the waxing rakṣas.

sanskrit: indrāsomā pari vāṃ bhūtu viśvata iyaṃ matiḥ kakṣyāśveva vājinā | yāṃ vāṃ hotrāṃ pari hiṇomi medhayā- -imā brahmāṇi nṛpatīva jinvatam ||
english: O Indra and Soma, let this thought encompass you on all sides like a girth around prize steeds. The oblation-invocation I send forth to you with insight — invigorate these sacred formulations, as a king invigorates his men.

sanskrit: prati smarethāṃ tujayadbhir evair hataṃ druho rakṣaso bhaṅgurāvataḥ | indrāsomā duṣkṛte mā sugaṃ bhūd yo mā kadā cid abhidāsati druhuḥ ||
english: Remember it back with your vigorous courses — slain, the rakṣas of treachery, the Bhaṅgurāvat demon. O Indra and Soma, let there be no easy passage for the evildoer, for that deceitful one who would ever assail me.

sanskrit: yo mā pākena manasā carantam abhicaṣṭe anṛtebhir vacobhiḥ | āpa iva kāśinā saṃgṛbhītā asann astv asata indra vaktā ||
english: Whoever denounces me as I go about with a guileless mind, denounces me with false words — may he be seized like water by a gleaming vessel; may the speaker of falsehood be shown to be a speaker of falsehood, O Indra.

sanskrit: ye pākaśaṃsaṃ viharanta evair ye vā bhadraṃ dūṣayanti svadhābhiḥ | ahaye vā tān pradadātu soma ā vā dadhātu nirṛter upasthe ||
english: Those who scatter naive speech about with their courses, or who corrupt what is auspicious with their practised powers — let Soma give them over to the serpent, or let him place them in the lap of Nirṛti.

sanskrit: yo no rasaṃ dipsati pitvo agne yo aśvānāṃ yo gavāṃ yas tanūnām | ripu stena steyakṛd dabhram etu ni ṣa hīyatāṃ tanvā tanā ca ||
english: Whoever would harm the sap of our food, O Agni — of horses, of cattle, of bodies — let that enemy, that thief, that committer of theft, go forth diminished; let him be abandoned here with his body and his progeny.
